evidence_articles.rephrased: **M.K. Stalin**, DMK president and Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, unveiled a new manifesto for the upcoming Assembly elections, promising various welfare schemes. The "Illatharasi Scheme" will provide non
evidence_articles.content: Releasing what he described as a “Superstar” manifesto for the Tamil Nadu Assembly elections on Sunday (March 29, 2026), DMK President and Chief Minister M.K. Stalin announced the Illatharasi Scheme under which all non-income tax assessee housewives will be given a coupon valued at ₹8,000 to purchase or replace household electronic appliances. They can choose from a range of appliances including a washing machine, a TV, a grinder, a fridge, mixies microwave oven and an induction stove. Follow updates for the Assembly elections 2026 “The DMK’s election manifesto has always been a hero. The manifesto is also the heroine of the election. Now the manifesto will enter the fray as a superstar,” he said, adding the coupon would be the better way to serve homemakers. “Otherwise, they will spend the money,” he told journalists at Anna Arivalayam, the party headquarters in Chennai. When asked whether the government would have funds to implement the new schemes, Mr. Stalin said similar doubts were raised in the 2021 election, but the DMK government fulfilled all its promises. Mr. Stalin also said the Chief Minister’s Breakfast Scheme will be extended to students up to class 8. It is now being implemented for the benefit of student of 1 to 5th standard. He also announced that the Kalaignar Magalir Urimai Thoagai for women heads of families will be increased to ₹2000 from ₹1000. The old age pension scheme will be increased from ₹1200 to ₹2000. In the case of the differently abled the amount will be ₹2,500. Mr. Stalin also announced that a free meter would be fixed for farmers who were getting free electricity. The annual salary limit for the Chief Minister’s insurance scheme would be ₹5 lakh per year, and the insurance amount would be ₹10 lakh. Published - March 29, 2026 07:25 pm IST

Joseph Vijay**’s **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, believing they missed a chance to rejuvenate the party in Tamil Nadu.  Some members suggest leaving the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance immediately and forming an alliance with the TVK if needed to prevent the BJP from coming to power. The TNCC president has demanded an explanation from the Income Tax department after footage showed officials raiding his office, contradicting their claims of no raids.

recent_articles.title: Assembly Elections 2026 LIVE: ECI orders suspension of Hingalganj OC over 'bias' in West Bengal - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** ordered the suspension of **Sandip Sarkar**, officer-in-charge of the Hingalganj police station in West Bengal, due to allegations of partisan behavior. The commission also issued new guidelines for handling surveillance cameras and video data after voting concludes in the upcoming Assembly elections.  These guidelines ensure that SD cards from polling booth cameras remain under supervision until further action is taken.

recent_articles.title: The Karur stampede is yet to fade from the memory of the voters at Velusamypuram - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Velusamypuram**, the site of a deadly political rally tragedy in September 2025, saw brisk polling on Thursday.  Voters were grappling with the lingering impact of the stampede that claimed 41 lives, including nine children, while awaiting answers about the cause and those responsible. **C. Joseph Vijay**, president of the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)**, was accused in the case but voters largely refrained from discussing it during the election process.  The polling station at Velusamypuram recorded 81.31% turnout with almost four hours remaining before closing.

recent_articles.title: State may witness close contests in many constituencies - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Tamil Nadu's** high voter turnout has raised questions about the closeness of this year's election results.  The 2016 contest, with a margin of victory of just one percentage point between the ruling AIADMK and the DMK-led coalition, serves as a precedent for potential close races in 2023. The **People's Welfare Front**, **Pattali Makkal Katchi**, and **Bharatiya Janata Party** contested independently in 2016, contributing to a wider margin of victory for the AIADMK.  This year, the presence of **C. Joseph Vijay**, founder of the **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam**, is expected to influence the outcome.

recent_articles.title: Stalin commends people of T.N. for record voter turnout - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Chief Minister M.K. Stalin** commended the high voter turnout of 84.69% in Tamil Nadu, which he described as a testament to the people's sense of responsibility and peaceful election process.  He praised voters for their dedication despite the scorching heat and emphasized that this was an election for a generation. **Mr. Stalin** concluded by stating that Tamil Nadu will win on May 4th.

recent_articles.title: Kancheepuram district sees over 87% polling - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Voting in the Kancheepuram district of Tamil Nadu was largely peaceful, with 87.39% voter turnout reported by 6 p.m.  **Siva** of Kuruvimalai in Orikkai attributed the high turnout to the DMK government's fulfillment of promises like pattas and good roads. **S. Ramesh**, an activist from Alancheri near Uthiramerur, highlighted the need for polling booths closer to villages due to poor road conditions.  Farmers at Keezh Kathirpur withdrew their protest after officials promised to expedite land document clearance.

recent_articles.title: Voting underway in key Indian states of West Bengal, Tamil Nadu - World - DAWN.COM
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Voting began in West Bengal and Tamil Nadu, with **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**'s **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)** seeking to gain ground in the opposition-held states.  In West Bengal, over 36 million people are eligible to vote as they cast ballots for members of the legislative assembly, with security heightened along the Bangladesh border. The campaign was marked by protests over voter roll changes and concerns about women's safety and corruption. In Tamil Nadu, polling is underway for the 234-member assembly in a single phase, with the ruling **Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK)** facing off against its long-time rival, the **All India Anna Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (AIADMK)**.  Results for both elections will be announced on May 4th along with results from Assam and Kerala, as well as Puducherry.

recent_articles.title: Will another film star be able to sway the election in India’s Tamil Nadu? | Elections News | Al Jazeera
recent_articles.rephrased_article: C Joseph Vijay, a film star turned politician, is seeking to become the next chief minister of Tamil Nadu.  He faces strong competition from the incumbent DMK leader MK Stalin and the AIADMK's Edappadi K Palaniswami. Vijay's TVK party, while attracting large crowds, lacks a clear political ideology and program that appeals to voters. The election is expected to be a three-way contest with Vijay potentially acting as a disruptor rather than a decisive victor.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu Elections 2026 LIVE: 37.56% votes polled till 11 a.m.; Vijay seeks two-hour extension of polling period - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: Over 5.73 crore voters in Tamil Nadu will cast their ballots on April 23rd in the crucial Assembly elections, with **Chief Minister M.K. Stalin** and **AIADMK general secretary Edappadi K. Palaniswami** leading their respective parties.  The high-stakes contest pits the DMK-led Secular Progressive Alliance against the AIADMK-led National Democratic Alliance, with **Tamil Nadu Chief Electoral Officer Archana Patnaik** assuring a smooth democratic exercise. Delegates from 17 countries will observe the polling process as part of the International Election Visitors’ Programme (IEVP) 2026.

recent_articles.title: Over ₹78 lakh in cash seized from DMK candidate’s aide in Mylapore - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sathiyamoorthy**, a personal assistant to **Dha. Velu**, the DMK candidate in the Mylapore constituency, was questioned by **election flying squad** officials after they seized over ₹78 lakh in ₹500 denomination notes and documents related to voter bribery from his apartment in Mandaveli.  The search, conducted with armed police security, uncovered bundles of cash, instructions for distributing money, and a cash-counting machine. The investigation is ongoing.

recent_articles.title: Over 12,000 police personnel to be deployed on polling day in Vellore, nearby districts - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Over 12,000 police personnel** will be deployed across Vellore, Ranipet, Tirupattur, and Tiruvannamalai districts for election-related duties on polling day. **The police** have roped in personnel from all wings, including the Armed Reserve, law and order, and traffic, as well as additional personnel from neighboring states like Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka.  Adequate security measures are being implemented to ensure a peaceful voting process, with vulnerable booths receiving double the number of security personnel.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Uthangarai constituency braces for a two-cornered contest - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Uthangarai constituency in Tamil Nadu is experiencing a two-cornered contest between the incumbent **AIADMK** MLA T.M. Tamilselvam and the Congress candidate Kuppusamy of INTUC.  The seat, known for its high proportion of Adi Dravidars, Aruthandiyars, Kuravars, and scheduled caste population, has been dominated by the **AIADMK** since 2011. Key issues facing voters include drought-related water harvesting projects, irrigation infrastructure development, mango price concerns, and demands for improved healthcare and education facilities.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Leemarose trying her luck in DMK’s pocketborough Lalgudi constituency - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Lalgudi constituency in Tamil Nadu is a key battleground for the upcoming Assembly elections, with **Leemarose Martin**, wife of lottery baron **Santiago Martin**, entering the race on the AIADMK ticket.  **K.N. Nehru**, principal secretary and Minister for Municipal Administration, backs **T. Parivallal**, DMK's candidate, while **Ku. Pa. Krishnan**, former AIADMK minister, is the TVK nominee. The constituency faces challenges like infrastructure issues, water scarcity, and rapid urbanization, with farmers contending with disrupted irrigation channels and a lack of access to drinking water.  The election outcome will likely depend on the candidates' ability to address these concerns and mobilize voters in this agrarian area.

recent_articles.title: Tamil Nadu election 2026: Is the ground under PMK shifting to favour TVK in Dharmapuri constituency? - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A three-cornered contest is shaping up in the Dharmapuri Assembly segment, with **Pattali Makkal Katchi (PMK)**, **Desiya Murpokku Dravida Kazhagam (DMK alliance)** and **Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK)** vying for victory.  **Sowmiya Anbumani**, the PMK candidate who contested the 2024 Lok Sabha elections in Dharmapuri, is a key player to watch as she seeks to build on her impressive performance against the DMK.
